title: Menu Reference
subtitle: Every item on the APRS Command menu bar — Settings, View, Map, Messages, Operate, Tools, and Help — and what each one opens.
in_this_chapter: How to read the menu bar
The Map menu (Draw and Weather submenus)

blocks.h1: What This Is / What It Is For

blocks.p: The menu bar runs across the top of the __map page__, just under the title bar. It is your master index to every window and dashboard in APRS Command. If you are hunting for a feature and don't remember where it lives, start here.

There are seven menus, left to right: **Settings**, **View**, **Map**, **Messages**, **Operate**, **Tools**, and **Help**. This chapter lists every item under each one, says in a sentence what it does, and points you to the chapter that covers it in full.

callout.label: Reading this chapter
callout.text: Menu names shown in **bold** are exactly what you see on screen. A menu item marked with a trailing ellipsis (like **Import GPX / KML…**) opens a dialog that asks you for more before it acts. Items with a small right-arrow are submenus that open a further list.

callout.label: Nothing here transmits on its own
callout.text: Opening a window from a menu never puts your station on the air. APRS Command is receive-first and starts with the **TX Disabled** badge lit in the title bar. Transmitting always takes a separate, deliberate action inside the relevant window.

blocks.p: **Settings** is a single item, not a drop-down. Clicking it opens the main Settings window, where your callsign, station identity, connections, map behavior, and audio all live.

rows: Opens the Settings window — station identity, connections, map, audio, and app preferences.

blocks.p: **View** collects the read-only monitors and dashboards — the windows you open to watch what is coming in — plus the light/dark theme toggle.

rows: Opens the Station List window — every station APRS Command has heard.
Opens the raw packet monitor — the unparsed text of each received packet.
Opens the telemetry monitor — decoded telemetry values from stations that send them.
Opens the events window — the running log of application and network events.
Opens the packet statistics dashboard — counts and rates for received traffic.
Switches the whole app between light and dark themes.

callout.label: Separator lines
callout.text: A faint horizontal line inside a menu just groups related items. In **View**, it sets **Toggle Dark Mode** apart from the monitor windows above it.

blocks.p: **Map** holds everything that acts on the map itself — drawing tools, weather layers, offline tiles, and the coverage and terrain tools. Two of its entries, **Draw** and **Weather**, are submenus that open a further list.

rows: Opens the on-map drawing toolbar — tools, color, fill, width, and measurements.
Loads lines, tracks, and waypoints from a GPX or KML file onto the map.
Saves your drawn shapes to a GPX or KML file.
Opens the weather window — reports from weather stations on the network.
Opens the National Weather Service alerts window.
Turns the animated weather-radar overlay on the map on or off. The label shows the current state.
Opens the geofence editor — define map zones that raise an alert when a station enters or leaves them.
Opens the offline map download window — save map tiles for use without internet.
Opens the coverage prediction window — estimated RF reach from a location.
Opens the elevation profile window — terrain cross-section between two points.
Opens the frequency reference window — a quick band and frequency lookup.

blocks.p: **Messages** gathers the tools for sending, scheduling, and tracking APRS text messages. Composing or scheduling a message stages it; it only leaves your station when you send it and transmit is enabled.

rows: Opens the Message Center — read and compose APRS messages.
Opens the broadcast window — send one message to a group of recipients.
Opens the scheduled-messages window — messages set to go out at a future time.
Opens the receipts dashboard — delivery and acknowledgment status of sent messages.

blocks.p: **Operate** is the on-air toolkit for running a net or activation — net control, objects you place on the map, and beacons. A separator sets the beacon and alert tools apart from the net tools above them.

rows: Opens the Net Control window — run a check-in net with a roster.
Opens the net script editor — write and edit the spoken script for a net.
Opens the object manager — place and manage APRS objects and items on the map.
Opens the session templates window — saved configurations for common operating sessions.
Opens the scheduled-beacons window — position or status beacons set to repeat.
Opens the shadow beacon window — beacon on behalf of another station.
Opens the alerts window — proximity, geofence, and rule-based alerts.

callout.label: Beacons put you on the air
callout.text: Everything under the beacon items in **Operate** is designed to transmit on a schedule. They still obey the master transmit setting — nothing goes out while the title bar reads **TX Disabled** — but review any beacon before you enable transmit.

blocks.p: **Tools** holds the utilities that don't fit the other menus — the internal event bus, session replay, RF diagnostics, reporting, the phone companion, training and traffic-simulation tools, the Direwolf modem profile, file-based integration hooks, and the exercise-mode switches.

rows: Opens the event bus window — a live view of internal application events.
Opens the replay window — play back a recorded session of received traffic.
Opens the RF diagnostics window — signal, decode, and modem health readouts.
Opens the after-action report exporter — summarize an operating session for the record.
Opens the mobile companion window — a URL and QR code for viewing on a phone.
Starts a fixed-port (8080), tokenless read-only station feed for the FieldCommand IMS tactical map on a trusted EMCOMM-NET. Shows the address to enter under the map's APRS Sources settings.
Opens the training window — run guided training scenarios and step-by-step tasks for operators.
Opens the simulation window — generate synthetic APRS traffic to exercise the app without live RF.
Opens the Direwolf profile editor — configure the managed Direwolf software-TNC modem.
Opens the file hooks window — configure file-based import/export integration folders.
Toggle Exercise Traffic Marking (tag transmit as EXERCISE)

Turns Exercise Traffic Marking on or off. While on, outgoing message and beacon text is prefixed with “EXERCISE” so drill traffic is unmistakable, and a badge appears in the title bar. This marks traffic; it does not block it — that is Exercise Mode.
Turns Exercise Mode on or off. While on, every transmit path is blocked for drills.

callout.label: Exercise Mode is a safety belt
callout.text: **Toggle Exercise Mode (inhibit all transmit)** is the switch to throw before a training net or drill. It hard-blocks all transmit so nothing you practice with reaches the air, on top of the normal transmit setting.

blocks.p: **Help** is where the built-in help, the keyboard-shortcut list, and version information live.

rows: Opens the About window — version, credits, and license information.

blocks.screenshot: The APRS Command menu bar directly under the title bar, with the Map menu open to show the Draw and Weather submenus expanded alongside the Coverage Prediction and Elevation Profile items.

bullets: **A menu item is grayed out.** The feature needs something set up first — usually a station identity or an active connection. Open **Settings** and finish your station setup, then reopen the menu.

**The radar item under Map ▸ Weather has a different label than shown here.** That item's text changes to reflect whether the radar overlay is currently on or off; the wording flips each time you click it. That is expected.
**I clicked a menu item and no window appeared.** It may already be open behind the main window. Check your taskbar or cycle windows before opening it again.
**I don't see a menu bar at all.** Make sure the main APRS Command window is focused and not covered by another window; the bar sits just below the title bar with the **TX Disabled** badge.

**A window opened but is empty or shows no data.** Read-only monitors under **View** only fill in once packets are being received. Confirm a connection is active in **Settings** and that stations are being heard.
